evals.prompt: I run Nordwind DevDays, a community-run CFP-driven conference in Hamburg. 320 attendees last edition, second edition is in May. Kestrel Cloud is our biggest prospect and their marketing director basically said they'd sign at the top tier if we hand over the attendee list and give their CTO a 30-minute keynote. I need to write up what sponsoring us is actually worth before I go back to her. Can you draft the value story?
evals.expected_output: A value-proposition draft for the brand buyer that opens with an explicit not-offered list (no attendee contact list, no purchasable speaking slot), deletes the pipeline category outright because the event is community-run, substitutes aggregate demographics for lead data, anchors on brand exposure, and carries the 320-attendee figure without inventing others.
expectations: Classifies Nordwind DevDays at the community-run pole and states which pole the benefit claims assume
Refuses to include an attendee contact list or any attendee contact data as a sponsor benefit
Refuses the purchased keynote slot, stating that sponsorship buys placement and access but never a program slot
Deletes the pipeline value category outright rather than demoting it, parking it lower in the menu, or reserving it for later
Gives a reason for deleting rather than demoting: a demoted pipeline promise reappears later as scope in the prospectus
Substitutes aggregate attendee demographics for lead data
Writes the not-offered list before drafting any benefit claim
States the not-offered items to the sponsor up front, before describing what the sponsorship includes
Names brand exposure as the default anchor category for this event
Identifies the marketing director as a brand buyer segment rather than writing one statement for Kestrel Cloud as a company
Does not produce booth size, logo placement or ticket counts as the value proposition
Does not set, suggest or negotiate a price or tier fee
Carries the 320-attendee figure through rather than substituting a different audience number

evals.prompt: We're putting together the sponsor story for Terrafold Summit, about 450 people, community-run, third edition. I want ONE tight value proposition we can use with everybody: recruiters, marketing folks, DevRel teams, whoever. I was going to lay it out as a value proposition canvas with the pains and gains on one side and our pain relievers on the other. Sound good?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of both the single blended statement and the canvas structure, replaced by the six-part per-segment template (Who / Why / What Before / How / What After / Alternatives) applied to one named segment at a time, starting by asking which segment to draft first.
expectations: Refuses to produce a single blended statement covering all sponsor buyer types
Explains that a blended statement dilutes into generic exposure claims no budget holder can route internally
Declines the value-proposition-canvas structure as the drafting frame
Gives a reason the canvas is rejected: it starts from the offer side and maps several segments at once
Proposes the six-part template instead and names all six parts: Who, Why, What Before, How, What After, Alternatives
Keeps the six parts in that order
Defines Who as a named budget-holding role, not a company
Names distinct sponsor segments to draft separately, including at minimum product-feedback buyer, recruiting buyer and brand buyer
Asks which single segment to start with rather than drafting every segment at once
States that What Before captures the status quo the segment uses today without the event
States that Alternatives names the competing events, channels or sponsorship products fighting for the same budget line
Does not present booth, logo or ticket entitlements as the value proposition

evals.prompt: Brackenhall Build is our first hackathon, never run it before. We have a monthly meetup that pulls 140 people and 210 on the waitlist for the hackathon so far. A fintech called Ollavant asked what return they'd get. I want to tell them we draw 400 developers and that sponsors typically see a 4x return on a hackathon. Draft me something convincing.
evals.expected_output: A first-edition value proposition that refuses both the 400-attendee claim and the 4x return figure, uses the 140-person meetup and 210-deep waitlist as honest demand evidence flagged as first-edition evidence, offers a named post-event-report commitment as a substitute, and labels each claim evidenced or aspirational.
expectations: Refuses to state that the event draws 400 developers, since no edition has happened
Refuses to quote a 4x return, or any other ROI multiple or conversion benchmark
States that this category has no published conversion benchmark to quote
Uses the 140-person meetup attendance and the 210-deep waitlist as honest demand evidence
Frames any attendance figure as an expectation derived from the meetup and waitlist, never as history
Flags the first-edition evidence as first-edition evidence inside the statement itself
Offers the organizers' own track record as a first-edition substitute
Offers a named commitment to deliver a post-event sponsor report as a checkable substitute for data that does not exist yet
Notes that no returning-sponsor rate, no prior post-event report and no prior attendee demographics exist for a first edition
Expresses confidence in the value without attaching a fabricated figure to it
Labels each claim in the draft as evidenced or aspirational
Does not invent a sponsor testimonial, customer count or past-edition statistic

evals.prompt: Helixon runs our own user conference: we own it, we fund it out of marketing, about 900 attendees, and we do opt-in badge scanning at booths so partners get scanned contacts back. A partner's developer-advocacy team wants to sponsor and their lead said what she really wants is to sit in on our roadmap planning and get her team's API in front of our users. What's the value proposition for her?
evals.expected_output: A product-feedback-buyer statement at the vendor-run pole: pipeline and consented lead retrieval stay on the table bounded by consent, roadmap influence is refused outright, product feedback is the co-lead category delivered through structured contact formats, and the compliance cost of the pipeline category is flagged.
expectations: Classifies the Helixon conference at the vendor/foundation-run pole
Keeps pipeline as an available value category for this event rather than deleting it
Bounds any lead-retrieval or badge-scanning claim by attendee consent
Refuses roadmap influence as a sponsorship benefit
States that sponsorship money buys placement and access but never influence over the program or roadmap, at either pole
Identifies the buyer as a product-feedback buyer from the developer-advocacy title
Names product feedback as the co-lead category for this segment
Describes the feedback mechanism as structured contact with a technical audience, such as a workshop slot, a staffed table or office hours
Notes that this sponsor routes the feedback internally to product or engineering rather than to sales
Flags the compliance cost of the pipeline category: a consent flow, a data-protection review, and a contractual limit on the sponsor's reuse of the data
Notes that handing a sponsor attendee contact details is irreversible and cannot be recalled

evals.prompt: Second edition of Calderhaus Conf. I have maybe four hours of admin time before I start sponsor conversations, and we already have last year's sponsor roster and the published program from edition one. Registration opens in three weeks. What evidence should I actually go collect to back the value story?
evals.expected_output: The default-rung instrument set: returning-sponsor rate and program-content ratio computed now from records already held, plus two or three aggregate demographic fields added to the registration form before it opens, with the deep attendee survey explicitly ruled out at this effort ceiling and its promotion condition named.
expectations: Recommends computing the returning-sponsor rate from the existing sponsor roster
Recommends computing the program-content ratio from the published program
Justifies both as near-zero effort because they only count records the organizer already holds
Recommends adding role, seniority band and company-size band fields to the registration form before it opens
Identifies registration-form demographics as the instrument that compounds edition over edition
Advises reporting registration demographics in aggregate only
Caps the added registration fields at roughly two to three, naming form friction as a real cost
Does not recommend a deep attendee survey as the move at this effort ceiling
States that the deep attendee survey tops both the value and the effort axes, so efficiency never selects it by default

Names the condition that would promote the deep survey anyway: courting an anchor or presenting-tier sponsor whose diligence asks about buying influence, or a vendor-pole event where composition claims carry the price
States the efficiency ordering of the instruments explicitly rather than leaving it implied by list order

evals.prompt: Someone from our own community, she founded a four-person observability startup and has spoken at our meetup twice, offered to put in a small amount to sponsor Larkmoor Days. Honestly I don't know what to tell her we'd give her for that money. She's not going to hire anybody and she's not going to get leads out of 250 people. What do I even say?
evals.expected_output: A community-member-sponsor statement where community goodwill leads rather than sits as filler, with the promotion condition named, goodwill described concretely as standing, existing-user relationships and market intelligence, and her alternatives treated honestly as possible complements.
expectations: Identifies her as a community-member sponsor segment
Names community goodwill as the lead category for this segment rather than a residual or filler benefit
States the promotion condition: the sponsor is drawn from the community's own membership or strategically depends on the ecosystem
Describes goodwill value concretely as standing inside the community, maintained relationships with existing users, and market intelligence
Treats community goodwill as a value category distinct from pipeline, not a softer version of it
Names alternatives she is weighing, such as open-source project sponsorship or meetup hosting
Notes that those alternatives may complement rather than substitute, and says so honestly if this event is not her best channel
Fills the six-part statement for this one segment only
Does not recommend upselling her to a recruiting or lead-generation benefit
Does not treat the small amount as a reason to offer a thinner or vaguer value story

evals.prompt: Meridian Trust's early-talent team is our anchor prospect for Thornquay Conf, community-run, 300 people, 60% senior or above from last year's registration form. Our venue deposit is due in seven weeks so I need this money committed by then. Their head of early talent asked if they'd get access to a candidate database. Write me the recruiting pitch.
evals.expected_output: A recruiting-buyer statement that refuses a candidate database, states in the statement itself that recruiting here is conversation-based, carries the 300-attendee and 60%-senior figures as the composition proof point, re-ranks toward on-site payoffs because of the seven-week deadline, and names the sponsor's fully loaded cost.
expectations: Identifies the recruiting buyer segment from the early-talent title
Refuses a candidate database, resume database or scanned attendee list
States explicitly inside the statement that recruiting at this event is conversation-based
Names concrete conversation mechanisms such as a staffed table or office-hours slots
Carries the 300-attendee figure and the 60% senior-or-above split through as the composition proof point
Attributes that composition figure to last edition's registration data
Re-ranks the value categories because of the seven-week revenue deadline and says which answer moved which category
Names brand exposure and community goodwill as the compounding categories deprioritized by that deadline
Names the alternatives this buyer uses today, such as career fairs or sponsored job-board placement, and why each falls short for this job
Describes the After as a self-selected shortlist that has already met the sponsor's team
Names the sponsor's fully loaded cost - fee, booth build, travel, staff days - rather than staying silent on it
Does not set a tier price for the anchor package

evals.prompt: Sponsor renewals at Vantry Systems Days went from 8 of 11 down to 4 of 12 this year. I want to rebuild the value proposition for our practitioner sponsors and I want to benchmark it: what's the industry standard sponsor conversion rate I should be hitting? Also just send me the whole thing in one go, I don't have time for back and forth.
evals.expected_output: A refusal of the industry benchmark, replaced by two or three self-set observables (first-call coverage, objection log, statement reuse) each paired with the revision it would trigger, with renewal rate attributed to the whole relationship rather than this deliverable, and the statements validated section by section rather than delivered as one block.
expectations: Refuses to supply an industry-standard sponsor conversion rate or any external benchmark figure
States that value-proposition framing cannot be measured against an industry conversion figure
Proposes self-set observables instead, selecting two or three rather than all of them
Names first-call coverage as an observable, tied to whether sponsor calls open with questions the statement already answers
Names an objection log as an observable, with objections tagged by segment
States that a recurring objection is a defect in that segment's statement rather than a sales problem
Names statement reuse as an observable: whether the downstream documents quote the statements near-verbatim
Writes down the revision each chosen observable would trigger, before outreach starts
States that sponsor renewal rate reads on the whole relationship - delivery, report quality, relationship - and is not attributable to the value proposition alone
Declines to deliver the result as one block, requiring explicit approval section by section
Hands the finished statements and proof-point inventory off to the prospectus and rate-card steps rather than packaging or pricing them here
